title: Fallback Coordinator & Tokenized Capacity Policies for Regional Request Prioritization
creator: Rhea Patel
description: Problem statement: We need a deterministic, circuit-breaker-aware routing tier that enforces SLOs while minimizing cross-region degradation during capacity pressure. Current heuristics occasionally cause noisy cross-region bursts and slow failovers when a single region experiences a degraded tail. This ticket proposes a 'Fallback Coordinator' pattern plus per-region tokenized capacity ledgers to drive latency-based routing, geo-pin respect, and graceful load shedding.
background_and_context: SLOs: product-facing p95 <= 120ms and p99 <= 450ms for text-generation on hosted tiers. Observed failure mode: when us-east is overloaded, clients get aggressively hedged to eu-west producing increased p99s and higher egress costs. Existing steering uses simple latency buckets and static weights; it lacks coordination across fast circuit breaker decisions and workload budgeting. This design aligns with Dedicated and Private routing semantics (must respect customer geo-pin and data locality).
proposed_solution_summary: Introduce a distributed Fallback Coordinator service that maintains soft per-region capacity tokens, consumes tokens for admitted requests, and exposes a ranked region list per-request combining latency hints, token availability, and geo-pin constraints. Circuit breakers will mark regions as temporarily inadmissible and the coordinator will perform budgeted failovers with progressive shedding. Key ideas: tokenized capacity budgets, fast local caches for per-request decisions, fallback sequencing with backoff, and explicit telemetry for SLO regression detection.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end failover completes within 2x baseline p95 for 95% of requests during regional outage scenarios in synthetic test
P99 across global QPS does not regress by more than 15% in the canary region after rollout
Circuit breaker trips are visible in Console (per-region) and trigger coordinator retries and budgeted shed behavior
Supports per-customer geo-pin override with documented audit log entries
Automated chaos test (simulated node and network degradation) passes with no customer-visible 5xx spike above defined threshold
detailed_design_notes: Token model: each region maintains a token pool representing available admission capacity (units = admitted requests per second scaled by model class). Tokens are refilled by local autoscaler signals (target utilization -> refill rate).

Coordinator: lightweight gRPC control plane that aggregates sampled capacity hints and circuit-breaker states to compute an ordered region candidate list per-request. The coordinator is horizontally sharded by customer namespace for scale and failure isolation.

Local decision path: request hits edge -> consult local cache of ranked regions (TTL 200ms) -> attempt to acquire token from target region via fast token-binding RPC or adopt optimistic admit with async reconciliation if RPC times out.

Circuit breaker policy: two-tier breakers (soft: latency/error probation; hard: sustained error/TCP/failure) with exponential backoff and decay. Soft trips trigger progressive shedding rather than immediate ejection.

Geo-pin semantics: customer or project level geo-pin is enforced as a hard inclusion filter. If geo-pin region is unhealthy, fallback is limited to explicit allowlist in customer's config and audit log records decision.

Load shedding: when global token shortfall detected coordinator returns shortfall metadata; callers should degrade by returning reduced token limits, lower max tokens per request (prompt truncation hint) or 429 with Retry-After when safe.

Telemetry: publish per-region admitted QPS, token pool fill, refill_rate, token_acquire_latency, circuit_breaker_state, and failover_path histogram. Expose SLO burn-rate alerts and regression alarms tied to prompt test harnesses.
Fallback sequencing: prefer same-continent then proximity, then price-aware fallback (if enabled) while ensuring we obey customer geo constraints.

Backward compatibility: coordinator can operate in 'observed' mode where it only reports suggestions to current router for 2 weeks before taking control. This enables safe rollout without immediate behavioral change.
tradeoffs_and_alternatives_considered: Centralized vs. distributed coordinator: centralized simplifies global view but is a single point of decision latency. We opted for a sharded coordinator for lower latency and failure isolation.
Tokenized budget vs. straight util threshold: token model provides predictable admission economics and easy per-customer quotas; it adds complexity in refill tuning.
Aggressive hedging vs. budgeted progressive failover: aggressive hedging reduces tail for a subset but causes noisy cross-region load; progressive failover is kinder to global SLO and costs.
Use of existing service-mesh routing layer vs. new lightweight router plugin: chosen to implement as router plugin calling coordinator to keep change surface minimal and enable quick rollback.
implementation_plan: WIP design doc + diagrams (Confluence) - rfc-ready (link below)
Phase 1: Coordinator prototype (read-only compute of suggested ranked list) + metrics export. Run in 'observed' mode for 2 weeks.
Phase 2: Router plugin integration with optimistic admit path and token-binding RPC. Canary to 5% traffic across low-risk customers.
Phase 3: Enable circuit breaker integration and progressive shedding. Expand canary to 30% with mitigation runbooks.
Phase 4: Full rollout, post-rollout SLO watch, iterate token refill tuning and autoscaler feedback loops.
rollout_and_canary_plan: 0-2 weeks: Observability only. Compare coordinator suggestions with current routing decisions; run divergence analysis.
Week 3: Canary (5% traffic) for non-enterprise customers with no geo-pin. Monitor p50/p95/p99 and token_acquire_latency.
Week 4: Enable tokenized admission for canary, introduce limited shedding capabilities with soft thresholds.
Week 5-6: Expand canary to 30% including Dedicated small customers; enable per-customer geo-pin respect; run chaos tests.
Final: Full rollout with 48h guarded release window and rollback playbook.
runbook_high_level: If coordinator outages observed: flip router-plugin to passthrough to legacy routing (control plane fallback).
If token pools drain unexpectedly: reduce global cap by invoking emergency shed policy and alert oncall team. Postmortem and token calibration required.
If P99 regression >15% in canary: rollback tokenized admission and investigate token-acquire latencies and circuit-breaker misfires.
If geo-pin violation reported: audit coordinator logs, revert to legacy routing, and file urgent incident.

decisions: Use sharded Coordinator by customer-namespace to balance latency and isolation.
Adopt tokenized per-region capacity model with autoscaler-driven refill rates.
Implement progressive shedding (soft -> hard) rather than immediate region ejection.
Expose an observed mode for 2 weeks before active routing changes.
